title: Incheon to Seoul Late Night: AREX, Bus & T-Money Guide 2026
description: Arriving at Incheon Airport late? Get to Seoul via AREX Night Service, airport buses, or taxi. Includes T-Money tips & late-night transit info for 2026.
html:
Arriving at Incheon Airport late? Get to Seoul via AREX Night Service, airport buses, or taxi. Includes T-Money tips & late-night transit info for 2026.

Photo: Sgroey / CC BY-SA 4.0 via Wikimedia Commons

Photo: IR 스튜디오 (Korea Tourism Org.) — 인천광역시 영종구 운서동

Figuring out transport from Incheon after midnight? Ngl, it's a whole mood.

So you just landed at Incheon International Airport (ICN) and it’s like, 1 AM. The vibe check is kinda rough when you realize most public transport has clocked out. But don't stress too hard, you've got options. Honestly, getting to Seoul this late isn't as scary as it sounds, but you gotta know the moves. It's not like you can just hail a cab and have it be cheap, y'know?

AREX is your best bet (usually)

The Airport Railroad Express (AREX) is the GOAT for getting to Seoul, but its regular service stops running late. The last Express Train (the faster, no-stops one) from Incheon to Seoul Station usually leaves around 11:50 PM. The All-Stop Train (the one that makes, like, 12 stops) runs a bit later, with the last train typically departing around 11:45 PM.

BUT! There's a special late-night solution: the Airport Railroad Night Service. This is a lifesaver. It runs from around 11:45 PM to 3:45 AM, making fewer stops than the regular All-Stop Train and going directly to Seoul Station. It's not super frequent, maybe every hour, but it WILL get you there. The ride takes about 70 minutes. A ticket will run you ₩9,500. You can buy these at the AREX ticket counter in the airport arrivals hall.

Pro-tip: Grab a T-Money card while you're at it. You can buy these at convenience stores in the airport (CU, GS25, etc.) and top them up there or at any subway station later. It's way easier than buying single tickets and works on buses and subways all over Seoul. Trust me, you'll use it constantly.

Airport Buses: Hit or Miss

Airport Limousine Buses are comfy and will drop you closer to specific areas in Seoul. The catch? Most routes stop running by midnight or shortly after. Some limited late-night routes might exist, but they're rare and way more expensive than daytime buses. Think upwards of ₩15,000-₩20,000 for a single ride, and they might not even run past 1 AM.

How to check: Your best bet is to look for signs in the arrivals hall pointing to the bus ticket counters. They'll have schedules posted. If you're arriving super late, like post 1 AM, don't bank on the buses being your main option. It’s more of a gamble.

Taxi Life (The Expensive Version)

Okay, so if all else fails, or you just want the door-to-door service, there are taxis. Standard taxis are available 24/7. You'll find the official taxi stands just outside the arrivals hall. A ride to Seoul Station can easily cost ₩60,000 to ₩90,000+, depending on traffic and exactly where in Seoul you're going. It's the easiest, but definitely the most wallet-draining option. Maybe split it with friends if you can?

There are also International Taxis which sometimes have English-speaking drivers and can be pre-booked. Still pricey, though.

Where to find transit info in the airport

Don't wander around lost! When you exit baggage claim, follow the signs for 'Transportation' or 'Public Transport'. You'll see:

  • AREX ticket counters and station entrances.
  • Airport Limousine Bus ticket counters and stops (check the big departure boards for routes and times).
  • Convenience stores (CU, GS25, E-Mart24) to grab that T-Money card.

Honestly, the airport is pretty good at signage. Just keep an eye out for the little train and bus icons.

FAQ

Q. Can I buy a T-Money card late at night?
A. Yes! Convenience stores like CU and GS25 inside the airport are usually open 24/7. You can buy and top up your T-Money card there.

Q. How much is the AREX Night Service?
A. It's ₩9,500 for a one-way ticket to Seoul Station.

Q. What if my flight is delayed and I miss the last AREX/Bus?
A. Your main options are the late-night AREX service (if it's still running) or a taxi. Taxis are always available but will be the most expensive choice.

Q. Is it safe to travel alone late at night in Korea?
A. Generally, yes. South Korea is known for being very safe, even late at night. Public transport areas are well-lit and monitored. Still, always be aware of your surroundings, especially when taking a taxi.
